name: TypeScript
desc: Static types over JavaScript. Use when a codebase outlives one person or one month.

name: JavaScript
desc: The language every browser already runs. Use when you want zero build step.

name: Node.js
desc: JS on the server. Use when you want the largest package ecosystem on earth and boring stability.

name: Bun
desc: Fast runtime with bundler, test runner and package manager built in. Use when you want one binary instead of five tools.

name: Deno
desc: Secure-by-default runtime with native TypeScript. Use when sandboxed permissions matter.

name: Python
desc: Use for data work, scripting and ML, where readability beats raw speed.

name: Go
desc: One static binary, real concurrency, fast compiles. Use for network services and CLIs.

name: Rust
desc: Memory safety without a garbage collector. Use when performance is the feature and crashes are not an option.

name: Java
desc: Use for large enterprise services where the JVM, the tooling and the hiring pool already exist.

name: Kotlin
desc: Modern JVM language. Use for Android, and for Java services you want far less boilerplate in.

name: C# / .NET
desc: Use in Microsoft shops, for Windows tooling, Unity games, or high-performance managed services.

name: PHP
desc: Use when shared hosting, WordPress or Laravel is the shortest path to a live site.

name: Ruby
desc: Use with Rails when one developer has to ship a whole CRUD product this week.

name: Elixir
desc: BEAM concurrency and fault tolerance. Use for real-time systems holding many open connections.

name: Swift
desc: Use for native Apple platforms when you want every iOS and macOS API on day one.

name: Dart
desc: The language Flutter runs on. Use it if you are using Flutter, and otherwise do not.

name: SQL
desc: The query language every relational database speaks. Use when your data has relationships worth enforcing.
